source.data_source: Schäfer, M. and Turek, S. (with Durst, F., Krause, E., Rannacher, R.), 'Benchmark Computations of Laminar Flow Around a Cylinder', in Flow Simulation with High-Performance Computers II, Notes on Numerical Fluid Mechanics 48:547-566, Vieweg (1996). DOI:10.1007/978-3-322-89849-4_39. Test case 2D-1: steady laminar incompressible flow around a circular cylinder (D=0.1) in a 2.2 x 0.41 m channel, cylinder centre (0.2,0.2), parabolic inlet Umax=0.3 -> Umean=0.2, nu=1e-3 -> Re=20. Quantity of interest: drag coefficient cD.
source.ref_data_source: FeatFlow DFG benchmark 2D-1 reference table (https://wwwold.mathematik.tu-dortmund.de/~featflow/en/benchmarks/cfdbenchmarking/flow/dfg_benchmark1_re20.html): the committee reference drag coefficient is cD = 5.57953523384.
source.reference_value: cD = 5.57953523384 (Schäfer-Turek / FeatFlow DFG benchmark 2D-1, steady laminar Re=20)
source.note: gt_value is the PUBLISHED committee reference (5.57953523384), NOT the bundled solver output. The included OpenFOAM simpleFoam laminar case (O-grid around the cylinder, ~25k cells, parabolic codedFixedValue inlet, forceCoeffs with magUInf=0.2, lRef=0.1, Aref=D*span) reproduces the reference within the T_good band; the agent must produce its own real OpenFOAM solve and read cD from the integrated surface force.
source.cd_definition_note: cD = 2 F_D / (rho Umean^2 D h) with Umean=0.2, D=0.1, rho=1, h=span. In OpenFOAM forceCoeffs: magUInf=0.2, lRef=0.1, Aref=D*span (frontal area), rhoInf=1. The Cd column index in coefficient.dat must be read from the header (do not assume), per of_forcecoeffs_column_order.

cd.description: Drag coefficient cD of the cylinder for the Schäfer-Turek DFG benchmark 2D-1 (steady laminar, Re=20), cD = 2 F_D / (rho Umean^2 D h)
cd.pass_tol_source: Flat 5% of |gt_value| — the single band every live track carries (#190, after #188 set it for combustion and battery). The band exists to catch a wrong configuration, not to grade numerical precision, and scoring inside it is binary. Widened from 4%. gt is the published Schaefer-Turek / FeatFlow DFG 2D-1 committee reference cD = 5.57953523384, not a solver output; the oracle lands at 5.5855, 0.11% away, so the widening costs no discrimination the case had. No recallable value enters the band that was not already at its centre — the committee reference IS gt. physics_min = 4.5 / physics_max = 7.0 bracket the confined-cylinder Re = 20 drag for this 2.2 x 0.41 geometry, so an under-resolved cylinder boundary layer, a wrong normalisation or Aref, a wrong inlet profile or a wrong nu still fall outside.
cd.kpi_quality_note: gt=published benchmark; anti-shortcut=OpenFOAM artifact gate. ANTI-SHORTCUT STATUS: STRONG. The DFG 2D-1 drag coefficient has NO closed form — it is set by the full pressure+viscous force distribution over a confined cylinder with a parabolic inlet at finite blockage, and is THE canonical Schäfer-Turek/DFG validation quantity. It cannot be inferred from an unbounded-Stokes/Oseen drag law or a flat-plate correlation (those neglect channel blockage and the parabolic profile). The value must be read from the integrated cylinder surface force in a converged field; a reported value with no polyMesh/ + non-zero time-dir U,p artifact scores 0 via the openfoam artifact detector. Doubly gated: tolerance band (no recallable formula matches at this blockage) + artifact detector.
cd.gt_value_source: Published committee reference cD = 5.57953523384 (FeatFlow DFG benchmark 2D-1 table; Schäfer & Turek 1996). T_good=4% T_bad=12% of gt; verified the unbounded-Stokes/Oseen recall values (cD_Stokes ~ huge, cD_Oseen for an isolated cylinder differ by >50%) lie outside T_good, defeating the analytical shortcut.

oracle_provenance.reference: Schäfer & Turek 1996 DFG benchmark 2D-1; FeatFlow reference table cD=5.57953523384

stopping.note: Stops on its criterion, at 3.3x headroom. Recorded because the number is not otherwise knowable without re-running: simpleFoam exits 0 either way and leaves the same fields behind, so a cap that had drifted below the criterion would look exactly like this one (#273, #286).

oracle_provenance.kpi_quality_note: gt=published benchmark; anti-shortcut=OpenFOAM artifact gate. Headline KPI cd carries full weight; mesh/numerical KPIs are weight-0 diagnostics.
